field.label: Enable
field.help: Record which LAN hosts used which ports and services, based on the firewall state table.

field.label: LAN interfaces
field.help: The subnets (including virtual IPs) of these interfaces are treated as your LAN / customer hosts. Their devices are also used for passive ARP listening (bridges are replaced by their members). In transparent bridge mode the interfaces usually have no IP address: add the customer subnets below.

field.label: Additional networks
field.help: Extra customer networks in CIDR notation, e.g. routed or bridged VDS public subnets (203.0.113.0/24).

field.label: Ignore firewall traffic
field.help: Do not record the firewall's own addresses as hosts, and skip connections the firewall itself started (including service tests).

field.label: Answered connections only
field.help: Only count connections the other side answered. Keeps port scans and unanswered attempts out of the statistics.

field.label: Record remote addresses
field.help: Keep per remote address detail (who talked to whom). Disable on very busy hosts to keep the database small.

field.label: Poll interval (seconds)
field.help: How often the state table is read. Connections shorter than this may be missed.

field.label: Automatic service test
field.help: When a LAN host is seen serving a port, connect to it from the firewall and identify the service (banner, HTTP, TLS, Redis, PostgreSQL, RDP, DNS, NTP...).

field.label: Tests per minute
field.help: Maximum number of ports tested per cycle (one cycle per minute).

field.label: Never test ports
field.help: Comma separated ports or ranges that are never connected to, e.g. 25,8000-8100. They are still listed by port name.

field.label: Use nmap
field.help: Use nmap -sV (version-light) first when /usr/local/bin/nmap is installed (pkg install nmap). Slower but recognises more services.

field.label: Alert on LAN to LAN traffic
field.help: Connections between two LAN hosts (e.g. one customer VDS to another) can indicate lateral movement. All of them are recorded and listed under LAN to LAN; this selects which ones also raise an alert (one per source, destination and port per day). Scans always alert unless this is off.

field.label: Trusted LAN hosts
field.help: Addresses or networks (e.g. backup or monitoring servers) whose LAN to LAN traffic never raises an alert. It is still recorded.

field.label: Also read the firewall log
field.help: Only useful when block rules log. Without logging, blocked traffic is seen through sampling and rule counters (see Blocked traffic below).

field.label: Scan threshold: hosts
field.help: Alert when one LAN host contacts at least this many other LAN hosts within 5 minutes.

field.label: Scan threshold: ports
field.help: Alert when one LAN host tries at least this many different LAN host/port combinations within 5 minutes.

field.label: Sample blocked traffic
field.help: Every poll, listen for a short, bounded time to connection attempts only (TCP SYN, UDP, ICMP echo) and check them against the pf state table: an attempt without a state was blocked. Cost stays fixed during an attack (time and packet cap), nothing is logged to disk. Numbers are estimates.

field.label: Sample interfaces
field.help: Leave empty for automatic: the LAN interfaces and, for a transparent bridge, every member of the bridge (attacks from outside arrive on the upstream member). On a routed firewall add the WAN interface to also see blocked inbound attacks.

field.label: Sample time (seconds)
field.help: Listening time per poll and interface. The poll takes this much longer.

field.label: Sample packet cap
field.help: Stop listening earlier once this many attempts were captured; protects the firewall during floods. The rate is scaled up accordingly.

field.label: Blocked outbound alert (pkt/s)
field.help: Alert when a LAN host sends at least this many blocked packets per second (spam, scanning, compromised host).

field.label: Blocked inbound alert (pkt/s)
field.help: Alert when at least this many packets per second towards one LAN host are blocked (attack in progress; critical at 10x).

field.label: Block rule alert (pkt/s)
field.help: Alert when one block rule drops at least this many packets per second. Exact, from the pf rule counters.

field.label: Track MAC / IP bindings
field.help: Read the ARP / NDP tables and alert when a MAC uses more than one IPv4 address, when a MAC changes its IP, or when an IP moves to another MAC (IP taken over, ARP spoofing, IP conflict).

field.label: Change window (hours)
field.help: A MAC using another IP within this period counts as an IP change (or as multiple IPs when both are active).

field.label: Ignore MAC addresses
field.help: Comma separated MACs that legitimately use many addresses, e.g. the upstream gateway (one IP per customer subnet) or a router doing proxy ARP. VRRP/CARP virtual MACs are always ignored.

field.label: MAC / IP source
field.help: A transparent bridge has (almost) no ARP entries of its own, so MAC / IP bindings are learned by passively listening to ARP and IPv6 neighbour discovery (tcpdump) on the selected interfaces.

field.label: States per LAN host
field.help: Alert when one LAN host holds at least this many firewall states (critical at twice the value). Typical for a DDoS target or a host flooding / scanning out.

field.label: New connections per second
field.help: Alert when one LAN host opens (or receives) at least this many new connections per second.

field.label: State table warning (%)
field.help: Alert when the pf state table is this full (critical at 95%). Increases of pf limit counters (memory, state-limit, src-limit, max-src-conn(-rate), overload, synflood, NAT map failures) and rules close to their "max states" always alert.

field.label: Watch pf tables
field.help: Alert when a LAN host appears in a pf table whose name contains one of these words, e.g. virusprot (connection limit overload), sshlockout, crowdsec.
